intent: To demonstrate the low survival rate of family businesses across generations.

units.meaning: The second-generation survival share for family businesses is 30% (0.30 of the whole).

basis.note: Table row gives value=30 and unit=percent.

accepted_routes: About 30% of family businesses survive to the second generation.
Roughly three in ten family businesses survive the second generation.
units.visual_evidence_rule: A donut/ring chart must visibly mark one segment as 30% or 0.30 for second-generation survival.
units.temporal_anchor: First clause: 'Only about a third of family businesses survive the second generation'.
units.reviewer_question: Must the exact 30% value be shown, or is an approximate three-in-ten wording sufficient?

units.meaning: The complement of the 30% survival share is 70%, meaning most family businesses do not survive to the second generation.

basis.note: Derived complement uses the table relative_value=0.3000.

accepted_routes: About 70% do not survive to the second generation.
Roughly seven in ten family businesses do not make it to generation two.
The non-survival share is 0.70, while survival is 0.30.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The complement of the highlighted 30% segment must be visible as 70% or as the remaining unhighlighted portion of the donut.
units.temporal_anchor: First clause: 'Only about a third of family businesses survive the second generation'.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video explicitly show the 70% complement, or is highlighting only the 30% survival slice enough?

units.meaning: The non-survival share exceeds the survival share by 40 percentage points: 70% versus 30%.

basis.note: Derived comparison: complement minus original share.

accepted_routes: Non-survival exceeds survival by 40 percentage points.
The gap is 40 points: 70% do not survive versus 30% who do.
Survival is 30%, non-survival is 70%; the difference is 40 percentage points.
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both the 30% survival segment and 70% remainder should be visible or labeled so their 40-point gap can be compared.
units.temporal_anchor: First clause: 'Only about a third of family businesses survive the second generation'.
units.reviewer_question: Is the 40 percentage-point gap between survival and non-survival required, or optional?

units.meaning: The displayed metric is a percentage/share of family businesses, not a raw count or absolute number.

basis.note: The table unit is percent and the entity is labelled 'share'.

accepted_routes: This is a survival share/rate, not a count.
The value is 30 percent of all family businesses.
The chart shows a percentage share rather than an absolute number of businesses.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must be a share/percentage visualization, such as a donut/ring, not a count bar or raw-count axis.
units.temporal_anchor: First clause: 'Only about a third of family businesses survive the second generation'.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video identify the metric as a percentage/share, or can it simply display the number?

optional_valid: The 30% survival share can be described as approximately three in ten family businesses.
The 30% value is the only table-supported survival figure for this clip.
The donut chart may visually de-emphasize the 70% remainder while highlighting the 30% survival slice.
unsupported_to_avoid: The narration's 50% figure for not lasting until the third generation, because it is not in the table.
Any third-generation, fourth-generation, 12%, or 3% survival values.
Raw counts of family businesses instead of the 30% share.
Causal explanations for why family businesses fail.
Calculating 15% as 50% of 30%, because the 50% is not table-supported.
Claiming the table proves exactly one-third (33.3%) rather than 30%.
notes: Only one table cell exists: share = 30% / 0.3000. The 70% complement and 40-point gap are arithmetic derivations; the narration's 50% third-generation claim is outside the table.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
